verdict.rationale: Hightouch Events documents that it collects behavioral events and stores them in the customer's warehouse. Identity Resolution writes unified identities and a one-row-per-identity Golden Record into the warehouse. A community source says data stays in the customer's own warehouse/S3 bucket. However, the documented schedule and trigger controls apply to outbound syncs, not to how events land, and no specific warehouse support is named. Missing for 10: documented user-controlled load schedule for event/profile landing, explicit support for Snowflake/BigQuery/ClickHouse/S3 as event destinations, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, raw events and profiles land in my own warehouse or lake (Snowflake, BigQuery, ClickHouse, S3) on a schedule I control

citations.quote: Hightouch Events collects customer behavior from websites, mobile apps, and backend systems, then stores that data in your warehouse.
Identity Resolution links related customer records into unified identities in your warehouse
Golden Record — a one-row-per-identity table of canonical field values
it all stays in the customer's own warehouse/S3 bucket
